title: Flatness over a base is detected after a faithfully flat intermediate extension
statement: Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $N$ be a $B$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with its $A$-module structure induced by $A\to B$, and suppose $C$ is faithfully flat as a $B$-module [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Give $C\otimes_B N$ its $A$-module structure through $A\to B\to C$. Then $N$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if and only if $C\otimes_B N$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general, line 8930), part (2), with R=A, S=B, S'=C, M=N; the same argument appears in the proof of Morphisms Tag 02JZ (lemma-flat-permanence)

proof.text: Faithful flatness detects injectivity of a $B$-linear map $g:P\to Q$: by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], the complex $0\to P\xrightarrow{g}Q$ is exact at $P$ if and only if $0\to C\otimes_BP\xrightarrow{1_C\otimes g}C\otimes_BQ$ is exact at $C\otimes_BP$. These two exactness conditions say respectively $\ker g=0$ and $\ker(1_C\otimes g)=0$, which are precisely injectivity. Here $C\otimes_B0=0$ because its pure tensors are all zero, by the defining bilinearity and generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $g$ is injective if and only if $1_C\otimes g$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat), item (2), applied to the three-term complex with first term zero; Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general), proof, faithful-flatness argument

proof.text: Put $N_C=C\otimes_BN$. For any $A$-module $U$, give $U\otimes_AN$ the $B$-action $b(u\otimes n)=u\otimes bn$. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the formula $\theta_U(c\otimes(u\otimes n))=u\otimes(c\otimes n)$ defines an $A$-linear map $C\otimes_B(U\otimes_AN)\to U\otimes_AN_C$. It respects $B$-balancing because $u\otimes(bc\otimes n)=u\otimes(c\otimes bn)$, and $A$-balancing because $(au)\otimes(c\otimes n)=u\otimes(c\otimes an)$. The reverse formula $u\otimes(c\otimes n)\mapsto c\otimes(u\otimes n)$ respects the same relations, so defines its inverse; the two composites fix every pure tensor and hence are identities. For an $A$-linear $f:U\to V$, the map $g=f\otimes_A1_N$ is $B$-linear, and $\theta_V\circ(1_C\otimes_Bg)=(f\otimes_A1_{N_C})\circ\theta_U$: both sides send $c\otimes(u\otimes n)$ to $f(u)\otimes(c\otimes n)$.

source.place: Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general), proof, tensor identification; the balancing calculation underlying Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), written out using the tensor universal property

proof.text: Assume $N$ is flat over $A$, and take any injective $A$-linear map $f:U\to V$. By the injectivity definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $g=f\otimes_A1_N$ is injective. It is a $B$-linear map by Step 2, so Step 1 shows that $1_C\otimes_Bg$ is injective. The commuting square with the isomorphisms $\theta_U,\theta_V$ in Step 2 then makes $f\otimes_A1_{N_C}$ injective: if it kills $x$, write $x=\theta_U(z)$, use the square to get $\theta_V((1_C\otimes_Bg)z)=0$, and apply injectivity of $\theta_V$ and $1_C\otimes_Bg$ to get $z=0$. Since $f$ was arbitrary, the same flatness definition gives that $N_C$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general), part (1) and forward direction of part (2), using the injectivity characterization rather than kernels

proof.text: Conversely, assume $N_C$ is flat over $A$ and let $f:U\to V$ be any injective $A$-linear map. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $f\otimes_A1_{N_C}$ is injective. Step 2 identifies $1_C\otimes_B(f\otimes_A1_N)$ with $\theta_V^{-1}\circ(f\otimes_A1_{N_C})\circ\theta_U$, a composite of injective maps. Apply Step 1 to the $B$-linear map $f\otimes_A1_N$ to conclude that it is injective. This holds for every injective $f$, so [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] gives that $N$ is flat over $A$. The two directions prove the asserted equivalence with the induced $A$-actions.

source.place: Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general), part (2), converse, using faithful-flatness reflection on the injection test
